name: Agency Toolkit
author: inspry

sections.description:
The Agency Toolkit plugin provides a lightweight way for agency owners, freelancers and website owners to quickly debug, optimize, and streamline the WordPress experience without needing a dozen or more additional plugins. This plugin came out of a need for our own agency to standardize the WordPress settings across all of our maintenance clients. This plugin saves time and maintenance by reducing the need for many other third party plugins and ensures only privileged users can access these settings.

Each setting can be enabled or disabled as needed to keep things light and customized to your own needs. Currently, we support the following with more to be added:

General Settings:

  • Limit the users who can view the Agency Toolkit Settings Page
  • Enable maintenance mode
  • Enable the WordPress debugger
  • Enable a custom agency footer with a name, URL and email in the WordPress Dashboard
  • Enable a custom agency logo on the WordPress login screen
  • Show Environment Indicator in Admin Bar

Security Settings:

  • Disable theme and plugin editors
  • Limit the users who can install and update plugins and themes
  • Hide WordPress version generator in front-end source code
  • Limit the users who can view Site Health
  • Secure the wp-config.php file using .htaccess
  • Stop User Enumeration
  • Checksum verification for WordPress core files
  • Limit users who can modify Admin Email Address
  • Override the Disable Admin Notices Individually to show all admin notices
  • Backend users summary: last-seen tracking and a REST summary of users by role, activity and Two-Factor enrollment, plus a list of administrator accounts unused for a year (Kadence Security optional)

Performance Settings:

  • Limit or disable post revisions
  • Disable emoticons
  • Disable pingback and trackback notification emails
  • Disable self-pingbacks
  • Disable XML-RPC
  • Disable Media Comments
  • Remove RSD links

Email Notifications Settings:

  • Disable admin notification emails
  • Globally change email sender
  • Disable WordPress Admin Email Verification prompt
  • Change admin email address shared in user emails
  • Receive email notifications when specific plugins are updated
  • Receive email notifications when specific plugins are activated and deactivated
  • Receive email notifications for WooCommerce payment gateways set in test mode (only works with Stripe, Authorize.Net, and PayPal Payments)
  • Receive email notifications if WooCommerce payment gateways have been disabled

You can also export and import plugin settings via .json file to ensure you have the same settings across all of your websites.

What if I lock myself out of the Agency Toolkit interface?

We have you covered. Simply go to ‘domain.com/wp-admin/admin.php?page=inspry-agency-toolkit&rescue=email’ where ‘domain.com’ is the WordPress website root domain and ’email’ is the email associated with your WordPress admin user account. This will send a new email to your email address with a link to reset the ‘Limit the users who can view the Agency Toolkit Settings Page’ setting. This way all WordPress admin users can access access the Agency Toolkit plugin interface. You can then re-select the users who should be able to access the interface in that setting.

See an option or tweak that you would find useful? Just email us and let us know.

Enjoy!
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin through the WordPress repository, upload the zip file via the WordPress Dashboard Plugins page or upload to your website’s plugins folder.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugin dashboard in WordPress.
  3. Customize to your needs in your WordPress Dashboard’s left sidebar under ‘Agency Toolkit’.
sections.changelog:
1.0.39

  • Change: Now requires WordPress 5.7 or later (was 5.5). Sites on an older WordPress keep working on 1.0.38 and are not offered this update.
  • Bug Fix: Maintenance Mode now answers visitors with HTTP 503 and a Retry-After header, the standard for planned downtime. It answered 500, which search engines and uptime monitors read as a broken site.
  • Bug Fix: Maintenance Mode no longer blocks WP-CLI or WordPress’s scheduled tasks (WP-Cron). Commands failed and scheduled jobs stopped while it was on.
  • Bug Fix: The inactive administrator list now includes accounts with no registration date on record (imported or migrated accounts). They were skipped before.
  • Improvement: Every setting is now cleaned when the settings form is saved, as WordPress.org requires. What is stored for a valid setting does not change.
  • Improvement: Code changes for WordPress.org’s Plugin Check: every file now uses the standard direct-access check, remaining admin text is translatable, and three outputs are escaped. No change in behaviour.

1.0.38

  • New: The backend users summary now lists administrator accounts with no recorded activity for a year (username, display name, email address and last-active date), so unused accounts can be reviewed. Activity includes signing in, application password use and WooCommerce REST API key use, and an account that owns a WooCommerce API key, an application password, the Google Site Kit connection or the Jetpack connection is marked so it is not removed by mistake. The list stays empty until activity has been recorded on the site for a full year. Every other part of the summary is still counts only.
  • New: The backend users summary reports whether the Require Two-Factor setting is on.
  • Change: The suggested privacy policy text (Settings > Privacy) now describes the inactive administrator list.

1.0.37

  • Bug Fix: Secure the wp-config.php file and Stop User Enumeration no longer raise PHP warnings, or show a permissions error that could not be fixed, on servers that do not use .htaccess (nginx hosts such as Pressable) and under WP-CLI. On those servers the .htaccess rule is skipped because it would have no effect; on Apache and LiteSpeed nothing changes.
  • Bug Fix: Stop User Enumeration now recognises its .htaccess rule when the rule is at the very start of the file, instead of adding it again.
  • Bug Fix: When .htaccess can be written but not read, those two settings no longer add their rule again on every page load. They show the permissions error instead.
  • Bug Fix: Turning Stop User Enumeration off now stops blocking ?author= links. They stayed blank with the setting off.
  • Bug Fix: Turning either setting off now removes its .htaccess rule even when the rule was written with a different site URL or in the older format, and no longer rewrites .htaccess on every page load when nothing changed.
  • Improvement: The Secure wp-config rule now uses the Apache 2.4 directive where available and the older one otherwise, so it no longer depends on mod_access_compat. LiteSpeed servers keep the original rule. Rules already in place are left as they are.
  • Bug Fix: Turning either setting off now also removes the blank lines its .htaccess rule added, instead of leaving them behind every time.
  • Improvement: Deactivating or deleting the plugin now removes its .htaccess rules, so deactivating it also clears a rule a server rejects. Settings are kept, and reactivating adds the rules back.

1.0.36

  • Change: Backend users summary (Security) is now on by default. It is switched on once, the first time 1.0.36 loads, on existing sites and new installs alike. Unticking it in the Security settings turns it off, and later updates leave it off. To keep a site off before it updates, run wp option update inspry_toolkit_users_summary 0 first, and do not save the Agency Toolkit settings until 1.0.36 is installed (saving replaces the 0). The summary is still counts only, for administrators only, and nothing is sent off the site.
  • New: The backend users summary’s last-active timestamps are included in WordPress’s personal data export and erase tools, Settings > Privacy suggests policy text for them, and uninstalling the plugin deletes them. Settings are kept on uninstall, as before.
  • Bug Fix: Stop user enumeration no longer raises a PHP warning on requests without a query string, such as WP-CLI and cron.

1.0.35

  • New: Backend users summary (Security, off by default). When enabled, records when each backend user (administrator, shop manager, editor, author, contributor) was last active in the WordPress admin, at most once per hour, and exposes a counts-only summary to administrators at /wp-json/agency-toolkit/v1/users-summary: users by role, last-seen age buckets, application-password holders and Two-Factor enrollment. No usernames or emails are included, and the requesting administrator is excluded from the counts. Two-Factor counts come from Kadence Security when it is active; without it they are reported as unavailable and the settings page says so.
  • Improvement: Function files now follow the WordPress filename convention, using hyphens as word separators. The option loader resolves both the new and legacy filenames, so existing files continue to load unchanged.

1.0.34

  • Confirmed: Compatibility with WordPress 7.1.
  • Improvement: Select2 and the Inter font are now bundled with the plugin instead of being loaded from third-party CDNs, so the settings page makes no external requests.
  • Improvement: Script and style versions now follow the plugin version instead of the current time, so browsers can cache them between page loads.
  • Bug Fix: Translation strings now use the “agency-toolkit” text domain so they can be translated. They previously used a domain that did not match the plugin slug.
  • Bug Fix: Prevent a PHP warning on requests where no host header is available, such as WP-CLI and cron.
  • Bug Fix: Escape the admin URLs printed in the settings page header.
  • Security: The settings import and export forms now require a nonce and the manage_options capability. Previously they could be triggered by a forged request against a logged-in administrator.
  • Security: The admin access rescue flow now requires a logged-in user, and starting a reset requires the manage_options capability. Previously the reset email could be triggered anonymously.
  • Bug Fix: The Site Health redirect now stops execution after redirecting, so the page cannot be read by ignoring the redirect.
  • Bug Fix: Imported user lists now contain only user IDs. Previously the exported logins were kept alongside the resolved IDs.
  • Improvement: Scheduled events are cleared on plugin deactivation.
  • Bug Fix: The admin access rescue confirmation notice now shows after the redirect that follows starting a reset. Previously the email was sent but no confirmation appeared.

1.0.33

  • Feature: Add optional Kadence Security force 2FA setup module.

1.0.32

  • Bug Fix: Admin email restriction now uses readonly instead of disabled to prevent profile update failures.

1.0.31

  • Bug Fix: Check for ToolKit Restriction status when displaying admin menu item. Prevents situations where disabling the option still restricted access.
  • Bug Fix: Add new selector for Admin Email input element.
  • Bug Fix: Respect WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE environment variable.
  • Confirmed: Compatibility with WordPress 7.0.

1.0.30

  • Only check for disabled payment gateways in the admin area.
